newsitem.title: INDIA: Tractors haul mangled bodies from air crash site.
newsitem.headline: Tractors haul mangled bodies from air crash site.

text.p: Tractors worked through Tuesday night to haul away scores of mangled bodies after the world's worst mid-air collision over northern India.
Near midnight, five hours after a Saudi Arabian Boeing 747 passenger aircraft and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 collided, most of the flames from wreckage lying in fields had been doused.
Villagers in this farming area, 80 km (50 miles) from New Delhi, joined rescue teams to carry away bodies on tractor- driven carts normally used to take cotton to markets.
The stench of burned human flesh mingled with the smell of aviation fuel and smouldering rubber and plastic.
Officials said all 350 or so people aboard the two aircraft were feared dead.
"There are no survivors," a police official said. "We thought we had three or four survivors but they died on the way to the hospital in Charkhi Dadri."
The United News of India (UNI) news agency said 275 bodies had been recovered so far.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) said rescue workers earlier battled flames to retrieve corpses from wreckage spread over a six-km (four-mile) radius.
PTI said more than 20,000 villagers had crowded around the crash site, where burning wreckage had gouged out a crater about 10 feet (three metres) deep.
The remains of the Saudi jumbo jet fell in fields around Kheri Sanwal village, near Charkhi Dadri which has a population of around 50,000 people.
Debris from the Ilyushin hit mustard fields in the nearby village of Malia Was.
Three rescue teams, including more than 300 policemen, had cordoned off the area, which lies in a sparsely-populated part of Haryana State.
"I saw three fireballs falling from the sky from a height of around 500 metres," local journalist Atul Singhal told Reuters.
Another eyewitness, Parveen Kumar, said: "I was standing at the bus stand when there was a flash and a big boom. After that there was complete silence."
A U.S. Air Force pilot flying nearby saw "two fireballs" plunge from the sky from the impact, at nightfall some 15,000 feet above northern India.

"In the distance off our right-hand side, two fireballs seemed to appear ... diverging away from each other," the pilot, who was bringing a military cargo plane into New Delhi, told reporters in Washington by telephone.
"The two fireballs proceeded to descend down and hit the ground and became fireballs on the ground," he said.
Officials said there were 312 people, including 23 crew, aboard the Saudi Arabian Airlines flight SV 763, a Boeing 747.
The plane was bound for Dhahran and Jeddah in Saudi Arabia. Most of the passengers were Indians and Nepalis.
The Kazakh Airlines flight KZA 1907 carried 28 passengers and 10 crew, according to transport officials in the Central Asian state.
It was flying from Chimkent in Kazakhstan to New Delhi but had been chartered by a company in neighbouring Kyrgyzstan and most of the passengers aboard were Kyrgyz.
